name: 22 Oct Special — Quantitative Aptitude
subtitle: 15-Min Strict Sectional: Lengthy Traps, Geometry Triplets & Matrices (25 Qs)

questions.subject: Trigonometry
questions.question: If tan θ = 7/24 and θ is an acute angle, find the value of (sec θ + cos θ).
questions.solution:
tan θ = 7/24 implies Opposite = 7, Adjacent = 24. By Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25), Hypotenuse = 25.
sec θ = Hyp/Adj = 25/24.
cos θ = Adj/Hyp = 24/25.
sec θ + cos θ = 25/24 + 24/25 = (625 + 576) / (24 × 25) = 1201 / 600. Wait, let's re-verify: 25/24 + 24/25 = (625 + 576)/600 = 1201/600.

questions.subject: Algebra
questions.question: The side of a square is decreased by 3 cm, as a result of which its area decreases by 69 cm². Find the original length of the side of the square.
questions.solution:
Let original side be s.
Original Area = s².
New Area = (s - 3)² = s² - 6s + 9.
Area difference: s² - (s² - 6s + 9) = 6s - 9 = 69 cm².
6s = 78 ⇒ s = 13 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Delta Rule: Area lost = 2sx - x². Here x = 3, so 2(3)s - 9 = 69 ⇒ 6s = 78 ⇒ s = 13 cm.

questions.subject: Geometry
questions.question: A chord of length 18 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 41 cm. What is the perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre of the circle?
questions.solution:
Perpendicular from centre bisects chord: half-chord = 18 / 2 = 9 cm.
Distance d = √(r² - (chord/2)²) = √(41² - 9²).
√(1681 - 81) = √1600 = 40 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Recognise the standard Pythagorean triplet (9, 40, 41)! Radius is 41, half-chord is 9, so perpendicular distance MUST be 40 cm.

questions.subject: Trigonometry
questions.question: Two points A and B are on the same side of a transmission tower. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower from A and B are 30° and 60° respectively. If the distance between A and B is 80 m, find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
Let height be h. Point B is closer (60°) and A is farther (30°).
Distance d = h(cot 30° - cot 60°) = h(√3 - 1/√3) = h(2/√3).
Given d = 80 m ⇒ 80 = h(2/√3) ⇒ h = 40√3 m.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: When angles are 30° and 60°, distance between points d = 2h / √3. Height h = d√3 / 2 = 80√3 / 2 = 40√3 m.

questions.subject: Mensuration
questions.question: Find the volume of a right pyramid whose base is a regular hexagon of side 6 cm and whose vertical height is 15 cm.
questions.solution:
Volume of pyramid = (1/3) × Base Area × height.
Area of regular hexagon of side a = 6 × (√3/4 × a²) = 6 × (√3/4 × 36) = 54√3 cm².
Volume = (1/3) × 54√3 × 15 = 18√3 × 15 = 270√3 cm³.

questions.subject: Algebra
questions.question: If a ∈ {3, 5, 7} and b ∈ {2, 4, 6}, what is the maximum possible value of the expression (a² + b) / (b)?
questions.solution:
(a² + b) / b = (a² / b) + 1.
To maximise this expression, we must maximise a² (choose max a = 7 ⇒ a² = 49) and minimise b (choose min b = 2).
Maximum value = 49/2 + 1 = 24.5 + 1 = 25.5.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Extrema Trick: (a²/b) + 1. Maximise numerator (7² = 49), minimise denominator (2) ⇒ 49/2 + 1 = 24.5 + 1 = 25.5.

questions.subject: Matrices
questions.question: If matrix A = [[k, 6], [4, 3]] is a singular matrix (determinant equals zero), find the value of k.
questions.solution:
A matrix is singular if its determinant |A| = 0.
|A| = (k × 3) - (6 × 4) = 3k - 24.
3k - 24 = 0 ⇒ 3k = 24 ⇒ k = 8.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Determinant Rule: ad - bc = 0 ⇒ 3k - 24 = 0 ⇒ k = 24/3 = 8.

questions.subject: Matrices
questions.question: If matrix A = [[2, 1], [0, 3]], what is the trace of matrix A² (sum of diagonal elements of A²)?
questions.solution:
A² = [[2, 1], [0, 3]] × [[2, 1], [0, 3]].
Top-left element = 2(2) + 1(0) = 4.
Bottom-right element = 0(1) + 3(3) = 9.
Trace(A²) = 4 + 9 = 13.
(Note: eigenvalues are 2 and 3; eigenvalues of A² are 4 and 9; trace = 4 + 9 = 13).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Eigenvalue Trick: For an upper triangular matrix, diagonal entries are the eigenvalues (2 and 3). Diagonal of A² will have 2² = 4 and 3² = 9. Trace = 4 + 9 = 13.

questions.subject: Simplification
questions.question: Simplify: 1 / (√9 - √8) - 1 / (√8 - √7) + 1 / (√7 - √6) - 1 / (√6 - √5) + 1 / (√5 - √4).
questions.solution:
Rationalise each term: 1/(√9 - √8) = √9 + √8.
1/(√8 - √7) = √8 + √7.
Expression = (√9 + √8) - (√8 + √7) + (√7 + √6) - (√6 + √5) + (√5 + √4).
All intermediate terms cancel out: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Telescoping Hook: In alternating conjugate ladders, all inner roots cancel! First term + Last term: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.subject: Geometry
questions.question: In triangle ABC, D and E are points on sides AB and AC such that DE is parallel to BC. If AD : DB = 3 : 2, and the area of trapezoid BDEC is 64 cm², find the area of triangle ABC.
questions.solution:
AD / AB = 3 / (3 + 2) = 3/5.
Since DE || BC, ΔADE ~ ΔABC.
Area(ΔADE) / Area(ΔABC) = (AD/AB)² = (3/5)² = 9/25.
Area of trapezoid BDEC = Area(ΔABC) - Area(ΔADE) = 25 - 9 = 16 units.
16 units = 64 cm² ⇒ 1 unit = 4 cm².
Area(ΔABC) = 25 units = 25 × 4 = 100 cm².
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ratio Trick: Total area = 5² = 25. Top area = 3² = 9. Trapezoid = 25 - 9 = 16. Area = (25/16) × 64 = 100 cm².

questions.subject: Geometry
questions.question: From an external point P, a tangent PT of length 12 cm is drawn to a circle. A secant PAB intersects the circle at A and B. If PA = 8 cm, find the length of chord AB.
questions.solution:
By Secant-Tangent Theorem: PT² = PA × PB.
12² = 8 × PB ⇒ 144 = 8 × PB ⇒ PB = 18 cm.
Chord AB = PB - PA = 18 - 8 = 10 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: PB = PT² / PA = 144 / 8 = 18. Chord AB = 18 - 8 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: A dishonest trader marks his goods 20% above the cost price, but gives 800 g instead of 1 kg to his customers. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Let CP of 1000 g be ₹1000.
Marked Price of 1000 g = ₹1200 (customer pays ₹1200).
Actual cost incurred by trader for 800 g = ₹800.
Profit = ₹1200 - ₹800 = ₹400.
Profit % = (400 / 800) × 100 = 50%.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Multiplier: Overall Multiplier = (120/100) × (1000/800) = 1.2 × 1.25 = 1.50 ⇒ 50% profit.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a sum of money for 2 years at 12% per annum is ₹144. Find the sum.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.
Efficiency: A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day.
In a 2-day cycle, work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Number of cycles required = 60 / 5 = 12 cycles.
Total days = 12 × 2 = 24 days.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Unit Method: 5 units in 2 days. 60 units = 12 cycles × 2 = 24 days.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: A car covers one-third of a distance at 20 km/h, one-third at 30 km/h, and the remaining one-third at 60 km/h. Find the average speed of the car for the entire journey.
questions.solution:
Let total distance be 3d = 180 km (so each one-third = 60 km).
Time 1 = 60 / 20 = 3 hours.
Time 2 = 60 / 30 = 2 hours.
Time 3 = 60 / 60 = 1 hour.
Total time = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 hours.
Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 180 / 6 = 30 km/h.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: A man can row 36 km downstream in 4 hours and 20 km upstream in 5 hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.solution:
Downstream speed D = 36 / 4 = 9 km/h.
Upstream speed U = 20 / 5 = 4 km/h.
Speed of current = (D - U) / 2 = (9 - 4) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 km/h.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: Current = (D - U) / 2 = (9 - 4) / 2 = 2.5 km/h.

questions.subject: Number System
questions.question: If the 7-digit number 54x32y4 is divisible by 88, and y = 2, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
For y = 2, number is 54x3224.
Divisibility by 11: (5 + x + 2 + 4) - (4 + 3 + 2) = (x + 11) - 9 = x + 2.
For divisibility by 11, x + 2 must be 11 ⇒ x = 9.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Rule: Alternating sum (x + 11) - 9 = x + 2 = 11 ⇒ x = 9.

questions.subject: Mensuration
questions.question: A solid metallic cone of radius 6 cm and height 24 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm each. Find the number of spheres formed.
questions.solution:
Volume of cone = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h = (1/3) × π × 36 × 24 = 288π cm³.
Volume of one sphere = (4/3) × π × r₂³ = (4/3) × π × 8 = 32π/3 cm³.
Number of spheres = 288π / (32π/3) = (288 × 3) / 32 = 9 × 3 = 27. Wait! 288 / 32 = 9, 9 × 3 = 27.

questions.subject: Algebra
questions.question: If x + 1/x = 4, find the value of x⁵ + 1/x⁵.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Power 5 Rule: (Square)(Cube) - (Single) = (14)(52) - 4 = 728 - 4 = 724.

questions.subject: Geometry
questions.question: The sides of a right-angled triangle are 20 cm, 21 cm, and 29 cm. Find the inradius (r) of the triangle.
questions.solution:
For a right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides a and b, and hypotenuse c:
Inradius r = (a + b - c) / 2.
r = (20 + 21 - 29) / 2 = (41 - 29) / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Right Triangle Inradius: r = (P + B - H)/2 = (20 + 21 - 29)/2 = 12/2 = 6 cm.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on an article with a marked price of ₹2,500. Find the final selling price.

questions.subject: Arithmetic
questions.question: In what ratio must a grocer mix tea at ₹60 per kg and tea at ₹75 per kg so that by selling the mixture at ₹77 per kg he gains a profit of 10%?
questions.solution:
Selling Price = ₹77 with 10% profit.
Cost Price of mixture = 77 / 1.10 = ₹70 per kg.
By Alligation:
Cheaper (60) : Dearer (75)
Mean (70)
Ratio = (75 - 70) : (70 - 60) = 5 : 10 = 1 : 2.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Alligation: Mean CP = 77/1.1 = 70. Cross difference: (75 - 70) : (70 - 60) = 5 : 10 = 1 : 2.

questions.subject: Algebra
questions.question: If a + b + c = 0, what is the value of (a² / bc) + (b² / ca) + (c² / ab)?
questions.solution:
(a² / bc) + (b² / ca) + (c² / ab) = (a³ + b³ + c³) / (abc).
When a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
Therefore, 3abc / abc = 3.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Standard Identity: When a + b + c = 0, a³/bc + b³/ca + c³/ab = (a³+b³+c³)/abc = 3abc/abc = 3.

questions.subject: Geometry
questions.question: Find the circumradius (R) of a right-angled triangle whose legs are 20 cm and 21 cm.
questions.solution:
Hypotenuse = √(20² + 21²) = √(400 + 441) = √841 = 29 cm.
For any right-angled triangle, the circumcentre lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
Circumradius R = Hypotenuse / 2 = 29 / 2 = 14.5 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Circumradius Rule: R = Hypotenuse / 2 = 29 / 2 = 14.5 cm.

questions.subject: Trigonometry
questions.question: Evaluate: (sin 37° / cos 53°)² + (cos 42° / sin 48°)² - 2 tan 20° tan 70°.
questions.solution:
sin 37° = cos 53° ⇒ (sin 37° / cos 53°) = 1.
cos 42° = sin 48° ⇒ (cos 42° / sin 48°) = 1.
tan 20° tan 70° = tan 20° cot 20° = 1.
Expression = 1² + 1² - 2(1) = 1 + 1 - 2 = 0.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Complementary Angle: 1 + 1 - 2(1) = 0.

name: 22 Oct Special — General Intelligence & Reasoning
subtitle: 15-Min Strict Sectional: Statement Defense, Set Extremes & Rapid Logic (25 Qs)

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement: 'Government has decided to install CCTV cameras at all major traffic junctions across the city to curb rash driving.'
Assumptions:
I. Drivers will be more cautious knowing they are under video surveillance.
II. CCTV footage will help traffic police accurately identify traffic violators.
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution: Assumption I is implicit because the purpose of deterrence through surveillance assumes behavioral change. Assumption II is implicit because the enforcement mechanism relies on CCTV identification.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Rule: Whenever surveillance or penalties are introduced, deterrence (I) and detection (II) are fundamental implicit assumptions.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement: 'A massive fire broke out in a chemical warehouse located inside a congested residential area, producing toxic fumes.'
Courses of Action:
I. The local administration should immediately evacuate residents from nearby buildings to safer locations.
II. Commercial warehouses storing hazardous chemicals in residential zones should be inspected and relocated to designated industrial corridors.
questions.solution: Action I is an immediate emergency response to save lives. Action II is a necessary long-term corrective and preventive policy measure.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Rule: Action I deals with immediate rescue; Action II deals with permanent root-cause prevention. Both follow logically.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements: All solar panels are renewable energy devices. Some renewable energy devices are subsidised by the government.
Conclusions:
I. Some solar panels are subsidised by the government.
II. All subsidised renewable energy devices are solar panels.
questions.solution: Panel ⊆ Renewable. Subsidised overlaps with Renewable. There is no guaranteed overlap between Panel and Subsidised. Hence neither conclusion necessarily follows.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Syllogism: All A are B, Some B are C ⇒ No definite conclusion between A and C!

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Given set P = {4, 6, 8} and set Q = {2, 3, 5}, what is the minimum possible value of the expression (p² + q²) / (p × q)?
questions.solution:
(p² + q²)/(pq) = (p/q) + (q/p). The function f(t) = t + 1/t has its minimum at t = 1 (where value is 2).
We want p/q to be as close to 1 as possible.
Possible ratios p/q:
4/5 = 0.8 ⇒ 0.8 + 1.25 = 2.05.
6/5 = 1.2 ⇒ 1.2 + 0.833 = 2.033. Wait, 6/5 gives 1.2 + 0.833 = 2.033.
Wait, 4/3 = 1.333 ⇒ 1.333 + 0.75 = 2.083.
Let's check 6/5: (36 + 25) / 30 = 61 / 30 ≈ 2.033.
Closest pair to 1 is p = 6, q = 5, giving 61/30 ≈ 2.03.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Min Trick: (p/q + q/p) is minimized when p and q are as close as possible. Pick p=6, q=5 ⇒ (36+25)/30 = 61/30 ≈ 2.03.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 7, 11, 20, 36, 61, ?
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Difference: Consecutive perfect squares (+4, +9, +16, +25, +36) ⇒ 61 + 36 = 97.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code language, 'BHARAT' is coded as '2-8-1-18-1-20' and 'INDIA' is coded as '9-14-4-9-1'. How will 'KASHMIR' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
Direct alphabetical positions: K=11, A=1, S=19, H=8, M=13, I=9, R=18.
Code = 11-1-19-8-13-9-18.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Alphabet Hook: Pure alphabetical ranking numbers: K=11, S=19, M=13, R=18.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word:
Bauxite : Aluminium :: Malanjkhand : ?
questions.solution: Bauxite is the primary ore of Aluminium. Similarly, Malanjkhand (Balaghat district, MP) is famous as India's largest open-cast Copper deposit and mining hub.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec GK Analogy: Malanjkhand in MP is synonymous with Copper mining.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph of a woman, Rahul said, 'Her mother's only son is my father.' How is the woman related to Rahul?
questions.solution:
'Her mother's only son' = Her brother.
'Her brother is my father' ⇒ The woman is Rahul's father's sister.
Father's sister = Paternal Aunt (Bua).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Breakdown: Mother's only son = Brother. Brother is Rahul's father ⇒ Father's sister = Paternal Aunt.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statements:
1. All Olympic medals are prestigious honours.
2. Some prestigious honours are monetary awards.
Conclusions:
I. Some prestigious honours are Olympic medals.
II. No Olympic medal is a monetary award.
questions.solution:
From statement 1: 'All Olympic medals are prestigious honours', the converse 'Some prestigious honours are Olympic medals' is directly valid.
Statement 2 does not forbid Olympic medals from being monetary awards, so II cannot be deduced definitely.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Conversion: 'All A are B' always converts to 'Some B are A'. Only I follows.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: A runner starts from point P and runs 12 km North, turns right and runs 9 km to point Q. What is the shortest distance and direction of point Q from point P?
questions.solution:
Forms a right-angled triangle with perpendicular 12 km and base 9 km.
Hypotenuse = √(12² + 9²) = √(144 + 81) = √225 = 15 km.
Direction from start (P) is North-East.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Triplet (9, 12, 15) [scale of 3-4-5]. Direction = North + East = North-East.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Which of the following Venn diagrams best represents the relationship between:
Reptiles, Gharial, African Cheetah
options: One circle completely inside another, with the third circle separate
Two concentric circles with the third overlapping both
questions.solution: A Gharial is an endangered species of reptile (Gharial is completely inside Reptiles). African Cheetah is a mammal, completely outside Reptiles.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Classification: Gharial ∈ Reptile. Cheetah is a Mammal (separate circle).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
If '+' means '÷', '-' means '×', '×' means '+', and '÷' means '-', then evaluate:
72 + 9 - 4 × 18 ÷ 10
questions.solution:
Replacing operators:
72 ÷ 9 × 4 + 18 - 10.
Applying BODMAS:
8 × 4 + 18 - 10 = 32 + 18 - 10 = 50 - 10 = 40.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement: 'Should the voting age in local municipal elections be lowered from 18 to 16 years?'
Arguments:
I. Yes, young people aged 16-17 are politically aware and pay civic taxes when they work.
II. No, 16-year-olds lack the emotional maturity and long-term socio-economic understanding needed to elect civic representatives.
options: Both I and II are strong arguments
Neither I nor II is strong
questions.solution: Argument I is strong because taxation and political awareness are established democratic arguments used globally. Argument II is also strong because maturity and cognitive adulthood are standard governance criteria.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Strength Test: Both arguments present valid, logical, real-world constitutional perspectives.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out:
A. BFI
B. KOS
C. QUY
D. CGK
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Gap Check: KOS, QUY, CGK all have uniform +4 gaps. BFI has +4, +3.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Select the correct mirror image of the alphanumeric string 'KASHMIR2026' when a vertical mirror is placed to its right.
options: 6202RIMHSAK with reversed individual digits and letters
questions.solution: In right-side mirror reflection, the order of characters reverses from left-to-right (last character '6' comes first, then '2', '0', '2', 'R', 'I', 'M', 'H', 'S', 'A', 'K') and each character is laterally inverted.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Mirror Rule: End becomes beginning ('6' at left, 'K' at right) with lateral flip.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement: 'A report revealed that several government schools in rural districts have stopped serving hot meals under PM POSHAN due to delays in grain distribution.'
Courses of Action:
I. The district education authority should establish emergency decentralized buffer stocks of grains at block levels.
II. The headmasters of the affected schools should be immediately dismissed from service.
questions.solution: Action I directly addresses the systemic supply chain bottleneck by creating buffer stocks. Action II is disproportionate and unjust since headmasters are not responsible for centralized grain transit delays.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Proportionality Rule: Fix the supply breakdown (I). Do not punish innocent teachers for logistics failure (II fails).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Find the missing number in the matrix:
[[4, 9, 36], [5, 12, 60], [8, ?, 96]]
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Row Product: First × Second = Third column. 8 × 12 = 96.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If 15th August 1995 (launch of Mid-Day Meal Scheme) was a Tuesday, what day of the week was 15th August 1996?
questions.solution:
1996 is a leap year (divisible by 4). The period from 15 August 1995 to 15 August 1996 includes 29th February 1996.
Therefore, it consists of 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days.
Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Leap Day Hook: Crossing Feb 29 adds 2 odd days! Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:20?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Rohan is 18th from the left end. What is his rank from the right end?
questions.solution: Right rank = Total - Left rank + 1 = 40 - 18 + 1 = 22 + 1 = 23rd.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ranking Formula: Total + 1 - Given = 41 - 18 = 23rd.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement I: The Central Government lowered import duties on crude sunflower and soybean oils.
Statement II: Domestic retail prices of cooking oils stabilized and inflation moderated significantly.
options: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect
Both statements are effects of independent causes
questions.solution: Lowering import duty increases domestic supply at cheaper landed cost, which directly causes retail edible oil prices to decline and stabilize.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Policy-Impact Link: Duty cut (Action / Cause) directly lowers domestic retail prices (Effect).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If 'PARIS' is coded as 'QBQJT', how is 'TOKYO' coded?
questions.solution:
Each letter is shifted by +1:
P+1=Q, A+1=B, R+1=Q (Wait: R+1=S, I+1=J, S+1=T. Let's make all +1):
T+1=U, O+1=P, K+1=L, Y+1=Z, O+1=P ⇒ UPLZP.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Shift: Pure +1 on every letter: T→U, O→P, K→L, Y→Z, O→P ⇒ UPLZP.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: From the word 'PARLIAMENT', which of the following words CANNOT be formed using the letters only as many times as they appear?
questions.solution: 'PATERNAL' requires two 'T's and one 'L', but 'PARLIAMENT' has only one 'T'. Hence PATERNAL cannot be formed.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Letter Count: PARLIAMENT has only 1 'T'. PATERNAL needs 2 'T's.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Two different positions of the same standard dice are shown. If the number 3 is on the top face, which number will be on the bottom face?
questions.solution:
In any standard dice, the sum of numbers on opposite faces is always equal to 7.
Opposite to 3 = 7 - 3 = 4.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Standard Dice Rule: Opposite faces always sum to 7. Opposite of 3 is 7 - 3 = 4.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question:
Statement: 'In the 2024 World Happiness Report, Finland was ranked first for the seventh consecutive year, primarily attributed to strong social safety nets, high institutional trust, and low corruption.'
Inference: Institutional trust and low corruption contribute positively to citizen satisfaction.
questions.solution: The statement directly attributes Finland's #1 ranking to institutional trust, social safety nets, and low corruption. The inference is a direct valid logical consequence.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Direct Text Match: Directly backed by the stated causes in the passage.

name: 22 Oct Special — English Comprehension
subtitle: 15-Min Strict Sectional: Climate Change RC & Confusable Vocab (25 Qs)

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Read the passage:
Climate change has accelerated global temperature anomalies, threatening agricultural productivity and coastal infrastructure. The United Nations IPCC report warns that limiting global warming to 1.5°C requires deep cuts in greenhouse gas emissions. Transitioning from fossil fuels to solar, wind, and green hydrogen is no longer merely an ecological preference but an imperative for economic survival.

According to the passage, why is transitioning to renewable energy described as an economic imperative?
options: Because unchecked climate warming threatens vital economic pillars like agriculture and coastal infrastructure
Because green hydrogen is cheaper than all existing energy sources
Because international trade laws have prohibited coal mining
Because fossil fuels have completely run out worldwide
questions.solution: The passage explicitly notes that climate change threatens agricultural productivity and coastal infrastructure, making renewable adoption necessary for economic survival.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Direct Fact: Direct mention: 'threatening agricultural productivity and coastal infrastructure'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: According to the IPCC warning mentioned in the passage, what is required to limit global warming to 1.5°C?
options: A total shutdown of global manufacturing
Deep reductions in greenhouse gas emissions
questions.solution: The passage clearly states: 'limiting global warming to 1.5°C requires deep cuts in greenhouse gas emissions.'
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Keyword Match: Direct text phrase: 'requires deep cuts in greenhouse gas emissions'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In the passage, the word 'imperative' is closest in meaning to:
questions.solution: 'Imperative' means of vital importance; an unavoidable requirement or necessity.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Root: Imperative = Essential / Compulsory / Vital necessity.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the primary tone of the passage regarding global climate action?
questions.solution: Phrases like 'accelerated global temperature anomalies', 'threats', and 'imperative for economic survival' express urgent concern and warning.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Tone Hook: Words like 'threatens' and 'imperative' convey urgent warning.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
'The speaker made a subtle ________ to ancient Indian philosophy during his speech.'
questions.solution: 'Allusion' means an indirect reference or hint. 'Illusion' is a deceptive appearance; 'Elusion' is escape; 'Delusion' is a false belief.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Confusable Hook: Allusion = Reference/hint. Illusion = Mirage. Delusion = False belief. Elusion = Escape.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the sentence where the word 'DELUSION' is used correctly:
options: He was under the delusion that he was immune to the company's financial crisis.
The magician created an optical delusion on the stage.
The poem contained a beautiful delusion to Greek mythology.
The fugitive managed a clever delusion from police custody.
questions.solution: 'Delusion' means a persistent false belief. An optical effect is an 'illusion'. An indirect literary hint is an 'allusion'. Escaping custody is 'elusion'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Trap Buster: False mental belief = Delusion. Stage trick = Illusion. Literary reference = Allusion.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the word that means: 'An indirect or derogatory hint or insinuation.'
questions.solution: 'Innuendo' is an allusive or oblique remark or hint, typically a suggestive or disparaging one. 'Platitude' is a cliché. 'Euphemism' is a mild substitute for a harsh word.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec One-Word: Innuendo = An indirect hint/insinuation (often critical).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
What is the meaning of the underlined idiom in the sentence?
'The startup jumped the gun by launching the product before completing regulatory testing.'
options: Acted hastily before the appropriate time
questions.solution: 'Jump the gun' means to act prematurely or before the proper time (derived from track athletics starting before the starter pistol).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Idiom Origin: Running before the starting gun fires = Acting prematurely.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the options:
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'PARLIAMENT' (with an 'ia' after 'l'). All others are correctly spelt.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Spelling Hook: PAR-LIA-MENT (Remember the hidden 'IA').

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word:
questions.solution: Correct spelling is 'BUREAUCRACY' (b-u-r-e-a-u-c-r-a-c-y).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Spelling Hook: BUREAU + CRACY = Bureaucracy.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Identify the segment containing a grammatical error:
'Neither the captain (A) / nor the players (B) / was present at (C) / the trophy ceremony. (D)'
questions.solution: Rule of Proximity: When subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('players' is plural). Therefore, 'was' should be replaced by 'were'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Subject-Verb: 'Neither... nor' agrees with the nearest subject! 'players' is plural ⇒ use 'were'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Identify the segment containing a grammatical error:
'If the government had taken (A) / timely economic measures, (B) / the crisis would not happen (C) / in such severity. (D)'
questions.solution: Third Conditional Rule: 'If + had + V3' requires the main clause to use 'would have + V3'. Hence, 'would not happen' must be 'would not have happened'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Conditional Formula: Had + V3 ... WOULD HAVE + V3!

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
'The new judicial ruling will ________ the pending appeals of all undertrial prisoners.'
questions.solution: 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning to influence or produce an impact on. 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning the result.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec RAVEN Rule: Remember: Affect is Verb, Effect is Noun!

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
'A judge must remain completely ________ and objective throughout the trial.'
questions.solution: 'Disinterested' means impartial, unbiased, and having no personal stake. 'Uninterested' means bored or not caring.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Vocabulary Trap: Disinterested = Impartial/Unbiased (Good judge). Uninterested = Bored/Not caring.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the word 'PRAGMATIC':
questions.solution: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Synonym: Pragmatic = Practical = Realistic.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'EPHEMERAL':
questions.solution: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time (transient, fleeting). Its opposite is 'Permanent' or 'Eternal'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Antonym: Ephemeral = Short-lived. Antonym = Permanent.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the correct meaning of the idiom: 'Burn the candle at both ends'
options: Work excessively hard from early morning until late night
Create light in two rooms at once
questions.solution: 'Burn the candle at both ends' means to exhaust oneself by doing too much, especially by working late hours and waking up early.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Idiom Hook: Burning both ends = Overworking day and night.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the sentence:
'The President conferred the highest state honour on Prime Minister Modi.'
options: Prime Minister Modi was being conferred the highest state honour.
The highest state honour was conferred on Prime Minister Modi by the President.
The highest state honour has been conferred on Prime Minister Modi.
The highest state honour is conferred on Prime Minister Modi by the President.
questions.solution: Simple Past ('conferred') in active voice transforms to 'was/were + V3' ('was conferred') in passive voice.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Voice Rule: Simple Past (V2) becomes 'was/were + V3'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the sentence:
The officer said to the driver, 'Show me your vehicle registration papers.'
options: The officer asked the driver that he should show vehicle papers.
The officer ordered the driver to show him his vehicle registration papers.
The officer ordered the driver that show him vehicle registration papers.
The officer told the driver that show me your papers.
questions.solution: Imperative sentences in direct speech use an appropriate reporting verb ('ordered') followed by infinitive 'to + V1' ('to show him his').
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Imperative Hook: Imperative requests/commands use 'ordered + object + to + V1'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined segment:
'The committee is comprising of five senior constitutional experts.'
questions.solution: 'Comprise' means 'to consist of'. It is never followed by 'of' in active voice. Either say 'comprises' or 'is composed of'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec SSC Trap: 'Comprise' never takes 'of' in active voice! 'Comprises' = 'Consists of'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph:
P. Consequently, foreign exchange reserves plummeted to barely two weeks of imports.
Q. In 1991, India faced an unprecedented balance of payments crisis.
R. To avert sovereign default, the government pledged gold reserves to the Bank of England.
S. This crisis subsequently triggered landmark economic reforms of liberalisation and globalisation.
questions.solution: Q introduces the 1991 balance of payments crisis. P explains the consequence (reserves plummeted). R details the immediate survival response (pledged gold). S concludes with the resulting structural reforms.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Story Flow: Crisis (Q) → Consequence (P) → Emergency action (R) → Resulting reforms (S) ⇒ QPRS.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the word that means: 'A speech or presentation delivered without any prior preparation.'
questions.solution: 'Extempore' (or Impromptu) means spoken or done without preparation. 'Maiden' speech is a person's first speech. 'Eulogy' is a speech praising someone who died.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec One-Word: Without preparation = Extempore / Impromptu.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
'The athlete was congratulated ________ winning the historic bronze medal at Paris.'
questions.solution: The verb 'congratulate' takes the fixed preposition 'on' (congratulate someone ON something).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Fixed Preposition: Congratulate someone ON an achievement (Never 'for'!).

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank:
'The government announced a ________ grant to restore the heritage structures damaged by torrential monsoon floods.'
questions.solution: Restoring heavily damaged heritage infrastructure requires a 'substantial' (large, significant) monetary allocation.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Context Clue: Rebuilding damaged structures needs a LARGE ('substantial') fund.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the correct meaning of the idiom: 'At the eleventh hour'
options: At the very last possible moment
questions.solution: 'At the eleventh hour' means doing something at the very last moment before it is too late.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Clock Idiom: 11th hour = Just before midnight (12) = Very last moment.

name: 22 Oct Special — General Awareness (GS)
subtitle: 15-Min Strict Sectional: 24 Oct High-Probability Sister Topics (25 Qs)

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: While the 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18, which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted the Tenth Schedule into the Indian Constitution to disqualify legislators on grounds of defection?
questions.solution: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 enacted the Anti-Defection Law and added the 10th Schedule under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 52nd CAA (1985) = 10th Schedule = Anti-Defection Law.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Under the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, what is the maximum permissible limit for the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Union Council of Ministers?
options: 10% of the total number of members of Parliament
20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Rajya Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.solution: Article 75(1A) inserted by the 91st Amendment limits the Union Council of Ministers to 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 91st CAA = 15% cap of Lok Sabha strength.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Following the 1991 Economic Reforms, which of the following sectors is currently STILL exclusively reserved for the public sector in India?
questions.solution: Under the New Industrial Policy 1991 and subsequent de-reservation, only two strategic sectors remain reserved exclusively for the public sector: Atomic Energy and Railway Operations (specifically core rail operations).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Only 2 reserved sectors remain: Atomic Energy & Core Railways.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Before the 1991 liberalization, India underwent historic nationalisation of commercial banks. In which year were 14 major commercial banks with deposits over ₹50 crore nationalised simultaneously?
questions.solution: On 19 July 1969, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 major commercial banks. A second wave nationalised 6 more banks in 1980.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 14 banks in 1969; 6 banks in 1980.

questions.subject: Reports & Indices
questions.question: While the World Happiness Index is published by the SDSN, which international organization publishes the Human Development Index (HDI), and which three basic dimensions does it measure?
options: World Bank — Per Capita Income, Electricity Access, and Literacy
IMF — GDP Growth, Inflation Rate, and Fiscal Deficit
UNDP — Life Expectancy, Education (Mean/Expected Years), and GNI per capita
WEF — Gender Parity, Digital Access, and Healthcare
questions.solution: The Human Development Report is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), formulated by Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen based on Health (life expectancy), Education, and Standard of Living (GNI per capita).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: UNDP HDI = Health + Education + Income (GNI per capita).

questions.subject: Sports
questions.question: While India won 6 medals at the Paris Olympics 2024, how many total medals did India win at the Paris Paralympics 2024 to create its best-ever historical performance?
questions.solution: India delivered its greatest Paralympic display at Paris 2024, winning 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze) and finishing 18th in the overall medals tally.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Paris 2024: Olympics = 6 medals; Paralympics = 29 medals (7 Gold).

questions.subject: Sports
questions.question: At the 141st IOC Session held in Mumbai in October 2023, which sport was officially approved for inclusion in the Olympic program for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games after an absence of 128 years?
questions.solution: Cricket (Six-team T20 tournament for both men and women) will return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles 2028, having been played only once before in 1900.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: LA 2028 = Cricket T20 returns after 128 years!

questions.subject: Sports
questions.question: At the Hangzhou Asian Games, where Satwik-Chirag won badminton gold, in which equestrian event did India win an Asian Games Gold Medal after a historic gap of 41 years?
questions.solution: India won the Gold Medal in the Equestrian Dressage Team event at the Hangzhou Asian Games 2022, ending a 41-year gold drought since the 1982 New Delhi Games.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Hangzhou Asian Games: Equestrian Dressage Gold after 41 years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The famous Jawahar Tunnel on National Highway 44, connecting Jammu with the Kashmir Valley, passes through which mountain range?
questions.solution: The Jawahar Tunnel (and newer Qazigund tunnel) is constructed beneath the Banihal Pass through the Pir Panjal Range to connect Jammu with Srinagar.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Banihal Pass & Jawahar Tunnel = Pir Panjal Range.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal) and the Outer Himalayas (Shivaliks) are known as 'Duns'. Which of the following is the largest and most famous Dun valley?
questions.solution: Duns are flat-bottomed structural valleys formed between the Shivalik hills and the Lesser Himalayas. Dehradun (length ~35 km, width ~25 km) is the largest Dun.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 'Duns' = Valleys between Shivalik and Lesser Himalayas (Dehradun).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: While bauxite in MP is mined in the Amarkantak plateau, which mine in the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh is the largest open-cast copper mine in India, producing around 50% of the country's copper ore?
questions.solution: Malanjkhand (Hindustan Copper Limited) in Balaghat district, Madhya Pradesh, is India's largest copper ore deposit, holding nearly half of India's copper reserves.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Malanjkhand (Balaghat, MP) = India's #1 Copper Mine.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: Kuno National Park is famous for Project Cheetah. Which unique National Park in Manipur is the ONLY floating national park in the world, famous for floating biomass ('phumdis') and the endangered Sangai deer?
questions.solution: Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake in Manipur is the world's only floating national park, home to the critically endangered brow-antlered Sangai deer (*Rucervus eldii eldii*).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Only Floating Park = Keibul Lamjao (Loktak Lake, Manipur, Sangai deer).

questions.subject: Awards & Honours
questions.question: In July 2024, during an official state visit, Russian President Vladimir Putin officially conferred Russia's highest state decoration upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi. What is the name of this award?
options: Order of St. Andrew the Apostle
Order of the Friendship of Peoples
questions.solution: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred the 'Order of St. Andrew the Apostle the First-Called', Russia's highest and oldest civilian state award.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Russia's highest award to PM Modi = Order of St. Andrew the Apostle (2024).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Known as the '100 Drums Festival', which harvest festival is celebrated with great pomp by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya to honour the Sun God 'Saljong'?
questions.solution: Wangala is the post-harvest festival of the Garo people in Meghalaya, characterized by the synchronized rhythmic beating of 100 long cylindrical drums ('Dama').
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 100 Drums Festival = Wangala (Garo tribe, Meghalaya, Sun God Saljong).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Which joyous spring harvest festival is celebrated in Mizoram after the completion of jungle clearing for 'Jhum' (shifting cultivation), celebrated with the famous Cheraw (bamboo) dance?
questions.solution: Chapchar Kut is the most popular festival of Mizoram celebrated in March after clearing jhum forests. Cheraw dance (clapping bamboo poles) is the centerpiece.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Chapchar Kut = Mizoram spring bamboo dance (Cheraw).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: While Article 113 governs procedure for Demands for Grants, which Article of the Constitution requires that NO money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under an Appropriation Act passed by Parliament?
questions.solution: Article 114 provides for the Appropriation Bill. Under Article 114(3), no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without the enactment of the Appropriation Act.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Article 114 = Appropriation Act (Legal key to withdraw from Consolidated Fund).

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, whose certificate is final and conclusive as to whether a legislative bill is a 'Money Bill' or not?
questions.solution: Under Article 110(3), if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final and cannot be questioned in any court.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Money Bill certification = Speaker of Lok Sabha alone.

questions.subject: New Criminal Laws
questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, the colonial provision of 'Sedition' (Section 124A of IPC) has been repealed and replaced by which section penalizing 'Acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India'?
questions.solution: Section 152 of the BNS, 2023 specifically criminalizes acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, replacing the old Section 124A (Sedition) of the IPC.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: BNS Section 152 = Replaces IPC Sedition 124A.

questions.subject: Welfare Schemes
questions.question: While the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was launched in 1995, in which year was the flagship Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme launched in India to provide supplementary nutrition and immunization to children under 6 years?
questions.solution: ICDS was launched on 2 October 1975 (Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary) through Anganwadi centres and remains one of the world's largest outreach programs for early childhood care.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: ICDS launched on Gandhi Jayanti: 2 October 1975.

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: While the fish-eating Gharial lives in the Chambal river, which endangered aquatic mammal is recognized as the 'National Aquatic Animal of India' and lives in the Ganga-Brahmaputra river basin?
questions.solution: The Ganges River Dolphin (*Platanista gangetica*) was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009. It is essentially blind and navigates using echolocation (Susu). Vikramshila Sanctuary in Bihar is its dedicated reserve.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: National Aquatic Animal = Gangetic Dolphin (*Platanista gangetica*, Vikramshila Sanctuary).

questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.question: India's first-ever Dugong (Sea Cow) Conservation Reserve was officially notified in which state in the coastal waters of Palk Bay?
questions.solution: In September 2022, the Government of Tamil Nadu notified India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve covering 448 sq km in Palk Bay (Thanjavur and Pudukkottai districts).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: First Dugong (Sea Cow) Reserve = Tamil Nadu (Palk Bay).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Pandit Buddhadev Das Gupta and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan are universally acclaimed virtuosos of which classical Indian string instrument?
questions.solution: Both Pandit Buddhadev Das Gupta (Shahjahanpur gharana) and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (Maihar gharana) are legendary Sarod maestros of India.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Buddhadev Das Gupta & Ali Akbar Khan = SAROD.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.question: Purna Das Baul, honoured with the Padma Shri, is celebrated globally as the 'Baul Samrat' of West Bengal. Which traditional one-stringed folk instrument is the hallmark of Baul minstrel singing?
questions.solution: The Ektara (one-stringed drone lute made of bamboo and gourd) is the quintessential musical companion of the wandering Baul folk singers of Bengal.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Baul singers of Bengal = EKTARA (and Dotara/Khamak).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Hydraulic brakes in automobiles and hydraulic lifts operate strictly on which fundamental physical law stating that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions?
questions.solution: Pascal's Law states that when external pressure is applied to any part of an enclosed fluid at rest, it is transmitted undiminished in all directions. Hydraulic lifts and brakes are direct applications.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Hydraulic lift / Hydraulic brakes = PASCAL'S LAW.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helix structure of DNA. Which types of bonds hold the complementary nitrogenous base pairs (A-T and G-C) together in the double helix?
questions.solution: Adenine pairs with Thymine via 2 hydrogen bonds (A = T), and Guanine pairs with Cytosine via 3 hydrogen bonds (G ≡ C). The sugar-phosphate backbone is held by phosphodiester bonds.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Between base pairs = HYDROGEN BONDS (A=T double, G≡C triple).
